The det A(1) residual of S16-20 and the difference polynomial of S16-R18-02 are exact symbolic computations, and S16-20 already carried evidence_type computation. claim: The factored form of the difference between the printed and corrected readings, displayed in S16-R18-02 under a PROVEN label, carried the WRONG SIGN. The appendix printed minus one quarter z(q-1)(t-1)(4p + q^2 t + q^2 - qt - q); the true factorisation is plus one quarter of the same product. The appendix's own unfactored form, which begins 4pqt - 4pq - 4pt + 4p, is correct and is inconsistent with the factored form printed four lines below it. Corrected in this session.

claim: The cause of the sign error is diagnosable rather than arbitrary. The difference between the readings is exactly -z times the det A(1) residual, and the residual genuinely carries a leading minus one quarter. The sign was copied across from the residual without the flip the factor -z introduces. The appendix's claim that the two independent tests 'agree on the correction term for term' is correct, and is what made the wrong sign look right.

claim: The repair verifies against a control that discriminates. verify_repair parses the displayed LaTeX into sympy and compares it mathematically, so an equivalent rewriting would also pass and a transposed digit would not. The repaired appendix MATCHES; the pre-repair file at refs/ is REJECTED by the same check. A checker that passed only the repaired text would prove that it can read, not that it can discriminate.

claim: The LaTeX reader in verify_repair failed on its first run and said so, rather than concluding. It could not parse whitespace-separated implicit multiplication and reported READER FAILED for both the repaired and the pre-repair file, returning no verdict. Had it instead silently parsed part of the expression it would have compared something that was not the display. The repair was one rule covering both spellings of implicit multiplication, not a special case for the string that failed.
label: INSPECTED

claim: The source's determinant constraint is narrower than the appendix quoted it. Journal page 2637, folio read off the page, states that -theta_i^2/4 is the determinant of A_i FOR i = 0, 1, and normalises A_infinity separately as t/2 times diag(-1,1), giving det A_infinity = -t^2/4 with no theta_infinity in it. The appendix had quoted the constraint unrestricted, which would be false at i = infinity. Only i = 0 and i = 1 are used, so no result depends on it; the restriction has been added.
label: INSPECTED
